basic_info: 45-year-old male with chief complaint of dysphagia, particularly with larger food pieces, and chest pain upon swallowing
present_illness: Onset a few weeks ago, with pain localized to the chest during swallowing. The pain feels like a burning sensation, especially when swallowing larger pieces of food. It does not radiate elsewhere. No weight loss reported. No regurgitation. No prior evaluations or treatments for GERD or esophageal disorders. No change in appetite, but difficulty eating certain foods due to discomfort. No prior imaging or endoscopic evaluations of the esophagus or upper gastrointestinal tract. Patient is not familiar with barium swallow procedure. Dysphagia is more pronounced with solids, not liquids. No coughing while eating, no change in voice. Patient has not had any recent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy or barium swallow studies scheduled or performed. Over the past few weeks, the patient has been avoiding harder-to-chew foods like meat or bread, opting for softer foods like pizza or burgers, though even these sometimes cause discomfort. The patient has not experienced unintentional weight loss or vomiting, and has actually gained some weight;
past_history: No prior history of GERD or esophageal disorders. No known autoimmune conditions or exposure to caustic substances. Family history: No known esophageal disorders or gastrointestinal cancers.
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16, Temp 36.8°C. No acute distress. Chest examination: no tenderness or abnormal findings. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. No palpable masses. No lymphadenopathy.
aux_exam: No prior laboratory or imaging results available.
